Ionic liquid in a supercapacitor

The ionic liquid 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium hexafluorophosphate, [BMIM][PF₆], between two charged graphite electrodes: the cell of an electric double-layer capacitor (supercapacitor), which stores charge in the layers of ions at the surfaces of its electrodes. The electrodes are fixed, periodic in x and y, and the liquid is packed between them, with the composition of the first layer of ions on each electrode set by the charge of the electrode.

The packed system (drag to rotate, scroll to zoom), built in the Julia section below: the cathode (z < 7.7) and the anode (z > 62.7), the cations (blue) and the anions (red), and the periodic cell, closed by a vacuum gap beyond the anode.

Files: electrodes.pdb, bmim.pdb, pf6.pdb, and the input file supercapacitor.inp.

The structures

  • The electrodes: two blocks of graphite, of three graphene layers each (AB stacked, 3.35 Å apart), 39.36 × 42.60 Å, a whole number of cells of graphene, so that the sheets are continuous across the periodic boundaries in x and y. The surfaces of the electrodes facing the liquid are at z = 7.7 (the cathode) and z = 62.7 Å (the anode). They were built by the script electrodes.jl:
The script electrodes.jl (click to expand)
#
# The electrodes of the supercapacitor (electrodes.pdb): two blocks of graphite, of three
# graphene layers each (AB stacked, 3.35 Å apart), periodic in x and y (39.36 x 42.60 Å).
# The cathode has its layers at z = 1.0, 4.35 and 7.7 Å, the anode at z = 62.7, 66.05 and
# 69.4 Å.
#
#   julia electrodes.jl electrodes.pdb
#
using PDBTools

# Rectangular cells of graphene, of a x b = 2.46 x 4.26 Å: nx x ny of them
nx = 16
ny = 10
a = 2.46
b = 4.26
basis = [(0.0, 0.0), (1.23, 0.71), (1.23, 2.13), (0.0, 2.84)]   # C–C bonds of 1.42 Å
layers = [(1.0, 0.0), (4.35, 1.42), (7.70, 0.0),        # (z, shift in y of the B layers)
          (62.70, 0.0), (66.05, 1.42), (69.40, 0.0)]
atoms = Atom{Nothing}[]
for (il, (z, dy)) in enumerate(layers), i in 0:nx-1, j in 0:ny-1, (bx, by) in basis
    # The first three layers are the cathode, the others the anode
    if il <= 3
        resname = "CAT"
        chain = "A"
    else
        resname = "ANO"
        chain = "B"
    end
    push!(atoms, Atom(; name = "C", resname, resnum = 1, chain,
        x = i * a + bx, y = mod(j * b + by + dy, ny * b), z, pdb_element = "C"))
end
write_pdb(ARGS[1], atoms)
println(length(atoms), " atoms, cell of ", nx * a, " x ", ny * b, " Å")

  • The ions: the cation was built by Open Babel from its SMILES (obabel -:"CCCCn1cc[n+](C)c1" -O bmim.pdb --gen3d -h), and the anion, an octahedron with P–F bonds of 1.59 Å, by hand.

The numbers of ions

The periodic cell, pbc 39.36 42.6 100.0, has the electrodes and the liquid between them, and a vacuum gap of 30 Å beyond the anode. The cell is periodic in z too, so without the gap the anode would touch the periodic image of the cathode: the two electrodes would be a single block of graphite, a capacitor whose plates are connected. The gap keeps them apart, as in the simulations of electrode interfaces, which correct the electrostatics of a slab periodic in x and y only (or use Ewald sums periodic in two dimensions). Its width is the third side of the cell: the corrections of the electrostatics usually ask for a gap wider than the slab of the system.

The space between the electrodes available to the ions, given by free_volume (see Volume estimates), is 85900 Å³, which holds 250 ion pairs at the density of [BMIM][PF₆], 1.37 g/mL (284.2 g/mol per ion pair).

The electrodes carry charges of -10 e (the cathode) and +10 e (the anode): 9.6 μC/cm² on their 1677 Å², the order of the charges of the electrodes of supercapacitors. Each charge is screened by the first layer of ions on the electrode, the 8 Å nearest to it, which has 10 more counterions than coions:

Regionz (Å)CationsAnionsCharge
layer on the cathode7.7 – 15.73525+10
bulk liquid15.7 – 54.71901900
layer on the anode54.7 – 62.72535-10

Every region has the density of the liquid, in the volume available to its ions (free_volume again: 10300 Å³ in each layer, 65400 Å³ in the bulk). The whole system, 250 ion pairs, is neutral.

Command line

The input file supercapacitor.inp (click to expand)
#
# A supercapacitor: the ionic liquid [BMIM][PF6] between two graphite electrodes, periodic
# in x and y, with a vacuum gap closing the cell in z. The electrodes carry -10 e (cathode,
# z < 7.7) and +10 e (anode, z > 62.7), about 9.6 uC/cm2, screened by the first layer of
# ions on each electrode (8 A): 35 cations and 25 anions on the cathode, 25 cations and
# 35 anions on the anode. Everywhere the density of the liquid (1.37 g/mL).
#
# check_initial_placement
tolerance 2.0
output supercapacitor.pdb
pbc 39.36 42.6 100.0

structure electrodes.pdb
  number 1
  fixed 0. 0. 0. 0. 0. 0.
  radius 1.5
end structure

# The layer on the cathode: net charge +10
structure bmim.pdb
  number 35
  inside box 0. 0. 7.7 39.36 42.6 15.7
end structure

structure pf6.pdb
  number 25
  inside box 0. 0. 7.7 39.36 42.6 15.7
end structure

# The neutral liquid between the layers
structure bmim.pdb
  number 190
  inside box 0. 0. 15.7 39.36 42.6 54.7
end structure

structure pf6.pdb
  number 190
  inside box 0. 0. 15.7 39.36 42.6 54.7
end structure

# The layer on the anode: net charge -10
structure bmim.pdb
  number 25
  inside box 0. 0. 54.7 39.36 42.6 62.7
end structure

structure pf6.pdb
  number 35
  inside box 0. 0. 54.7 39.36 42.6 62.7
end structure

The electrodes are a single fixed molecule (see Fixed molecules), with the radius of their atoms set to 1.5 Å, so that the atoms of the ions are at least 2.5 Å from the carbon atoms. Each region of the table above is a box, and each kind of ion in it a structure block: the cations and the anions of the same region have the same constraint, and the composition of the region is given by their numbers. The whole ions are kept in their regions: the boundaries between the regions are planes, which the packing does not cross, and a simulation relaxes them.

Check the initial placement first

Uncomment the check_initial_placement line of the input file, and run it as below (see Checking the initial placement): the initial placement, written to the output file in a fraction of a second, has the ions in their regions, between the electrodes.

When it does (see the views in the Julia section), comment the line again, and run the packing.

Packing

packmol supercapacitor.inp

The packing (11840 atoms) takes about a second.

Julia

The electrodes, fixed, and the regions between them, in z:

using Packmol, PDBToolselectrodes = structure_type("electrodes.pdb";    number = 1,    fixed = ([0., 0., 0.], [0., 0., 0.]),    radius = 1.5,)cathode_layer = InsideBox([0., 0., 7.7], [39.36, 42.6, 15.7])bulk = InsideBox([0., 0., 15.7], [39.36, 42.6, 54.7])anode_layer = InsideBox([0., 0., 54.7], [39.36, 42.6, 62.7])

The ions of each region, with the numbers of the table above:

cations_cathode = structure_type("bmim.pdb"; number = 35, constraints = [cathode_layer])anions_cathode = structure_type("pf6.pdb"; number = 25, constraints = [cathode_layer])cations_bulk = structure_type("bmim.pdb"; number = 190, constraints = [bulk])anions_bulk = structure_type("pf6.pdb"; number = 190, constraints = [bulk])cations_anode = structure_type("bmim.pdb"; number = 25, constraints = [anode_layer])anions_anode = structure_type("pf6.pdb"; number = 35, constraints = [anode_layer])

The system, in the periodic cell of pbc 39.36 42.6 100.0 (from the origin), first with only the initial placement:

system = PackmolSystem(    [electrodes,     cations_cathode, anions_cathode,     cations_bulk, anions_bulk,     cations_anode, anions_anode];    output = "supercapacitor.pdb",    tolerance = 2.0,    unitcell = [39.36 0. 0.; 0. 42.6 0.; 0. 0. 100.0],    unitcell_center = [19.68, 21.3, 50.0],    check_initial_placement = true, # first, only the initial placement)packmol(system)system.status
:not_packed

The initial placement, with the visualize function of PDBTools.jl (drag to rotate, scroll to zoom): the ions are in their regions, but may overlap:

function show_system(system)    return visualize(get_atoms(system),        "resname CAT ANO" => (style = :sticks, color = "gray"),        "resname BMIM" => (style = :sticks, color = "blue"),        "resname PF6" => (style = :spheres, color = "red");        unitcell = UnitCell(system.unitcell),        rotate = [(:z, 30), (:x, -70)],    )endshow_system(system)

Then the packing:

system.check_initial_placement = falsepackmol(system)show_system(system)

To build the capacitor at another voltage, change the numbers of the layers: the charge of each electrode is the difference between the counterions and the coions of its layer.

get_atoms(packmol_system::PackmolSystem)

Returns the atoms of the packed system, with their current coordinates.

InsideBox(lower, upper; weight) InsideBox(; center, sides, weight)

Keeps the atoms inside an axis-aligned box.

PackmolSystem(structure_types::Vector{<:StructureType}; output::String, kwargs...)

Build a PackmolSystem directly from a vector of StructureTypes (see structure_type), without going through an input file.

packmol(input_file::String; options...) packmol(packmol_system::PackmolSystem; options...) packmol( system::SolutionBoxUS; output="system.pdb", # box size box_sides::AbstractVector{<:Number}, # or margin::Number, pbc::Symbol = :cubic, kwargs..., ) packmol( system::SolutionBoxUSC; concentration::Number, concentration_units::Union{Nothing,String} = nothing, output="system.pdb", # box size box_sides::AbstractVector{<:Number}, # or margin::Number, pbc::Symbol = :cubic, kwargs..., ) packmol( system::SolutionBoxUWI; ionic_concentration::Number=0.15u"mol/L", output="system.pdb", # box size box_sides::AbstractVector{<:Number}, # or margin::Number, pbc::Symbol = :cubic, kwargs..., ) packmol( system::Membrane; output="membrane.pdb", kwargs..., ) packmol(system::MembraneProtein; output = "membrane_protein.pdb", kwargs...)

Read a Packmol input file, run the packing optimization, and write the output.

structure_type(filename; number, constraints=Constraint[], tolerance=2.0, radius=nothing, fixed=nothing, center=:none, residue_numbering=-1, D=3, T=Float64)

Build a StructureType for number copies of the molecule read from the PDB file filename, without going through an input file.

packmol(system::MembraneProtein; output = "membrane_protein.pdb", kwargs...)

Builds and packs a membrane protein system, without writing an input file (as write_packmol_input followed by packmol).

packmol( system::Membrane; output="membrane.pdb", kwargs..., )

Builds and packs a lipid membrane system, without writing an input file.

packmol( system::SolutionBoxUSC; concentration::Number, concentration_units::Union{Nothing,String} = nothing, output="system.pdb", # box size box_sides::AbstractVector{<:Number}, # or margin::Number, pbc::Symbol = :cubic, kwargs..., )

Builds and packs a Solute + Solvent + Cossolvent system, without writing an input file.

packmol( system::SolutionBoxUS; output="system.pdb", # box size box_sides::AbstractVector{<:Number}, # or margin::Number, pbc::Symbol = :cubic, kwargs..., )

Builds and packs a Solute + Solvent system, without writing an input file.

packmol( system::SolutionBoxUWI; ionic_concentration::Number=0.15u"mol/L", output="system.pdb", # box size box_sides::AbstractVector{<:Number}, # or margin::Number, pbc::Symbol = :cubic, kwargs..., )
